items.description: CLAUDE.md documents `npm run test:unit` as the unit-test command, twice. package.json declares no test:unit script — the only test script is `test` (vitest run), and CI runs `pnpm test`. An agent following the instruction runs a command that does not exist.

CLAUDE.md states runtime configuration lives in `src/settings.ts` and that every environment value is read there. No such file exists; the loader is `src/config.ts`. This is a load-bearing path claim, not an illustrative example.

CLAUDE.md claims the stack is Express 4 with the classic middleware chain. package.json depends on fastify ^5.1.0 with no express entry, and src/server.ts imports Fastify. The framework claim is contradicted by the manifest.

AGENTS.md announces itself as a mirror of CLAUDE.md, but the two disagree on framework (Fastify vs Express), package manager (pnpm vs npm), and test command (pnpm test vs npm run test:unit). The mirroring itself is endorsed; the drift between the copies is the defect, and an agent's behavior now depends on which surface its tool loaded.

CLAUDE.md instructs installing with `npm install`. package.json pins packageManager pnpm@9.12.0 and CI runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. The documented package manager contradicts the repo's own.
CLAUDE.md states three services run behind the gateway. services/ holds four (billing, ledger, notify, webhooks). The fix removes the number and points at the directory rather than refreshing it.
CLAUDE.md points at AGENTS.md section "Testing" for testing conventions. AGENTS.md has no Testing section — its only sections are Stack and Essential commands.

Two claims in one sentence, both false and both settled inside this tree. package.json defines `db:migrate` as `psql $DATABASE_URL -f migrations/0001_init.sql` — one hard-coded file, not every file in `migrations/` in filename order. And `migrations/0001_init.sql` is a bare `CREATE TABLE payments (...)` with no `IF NOT EXISTS` and no applied-migrations table, so the second run errors rather than no-ops. The script name resolves, which is what carries this past a check that only asks whether the documented command exists.
